Patches to the vendored tailscale-rs crates
===========================================

What is here
------------
The folders here -- tailscale, ts_runtime, ts_control, ts_netstack_smoltcp_core, ts_derp,
ts_netmon and ts_dataplane --
are copies of the tailscale-rs crates of the same names, version 0.6.1 from crates.io, with
ThinkTerm's changes on top. The root Cargo.toml points crates.io's versions at them
([patch.crates-io]) and keeps them out of the workspace (exclude). Every other tailscale-rs
crate (ts_keys, ts_tunnel, ...) still comes from crates.io, held at the same version by
Cargo.lock.

Only thinkterm-tailnet/src/node.rs calls the library; the rest of ThinkTerm goes through
thinkterm-tailnet.

Finding our changes
-------------------
Every change is marked with a comment starting "ThinkTerm (<group>)", one of the groups
below:

    grep -rn "ThinkTerm (" deps/tailscale-rs --exclude=PATCHES.txt

The whole difference from upstream, at any time, against a fresh copy of 0.6.1:

    for c in tailscale ts_runtime ts_control ts_netstack_smoltcp_core ts_derp ts_netmon ts_dataplane; do
        curl -sL "https://static.crates.io/crates/$c/$c-0.6.1.crate" | tar xz -C /tmp
        diff -ru "/tmp/$c-0.6.1" "deps/tailscale-rs/$c"
    done

Upstream files this copy does not carry (README.md, examples, tests, Cargo.lock,
Cargo.toml.orig, .cargo_vcs_info.json) show up as "Only in", and so do the LICENSE and
PATENTS that ts_runtime, ts_control, ts_netstack_smoltcp_core, ts_derp, ts_netmon and
ts_dataplane got from the tailscale crate, as they ship without them. The ts_netmon
and ts_dataplane copies retain their upstream ancillary files. All of that is expected.

ts_netmon provenance
-------------------
Source archive: https://static.crates.io/crates/ts_netmon/ts_netmon-0.6.1.crate
SHA-256: 9db3f993efce5c30bd72dda4d9b2036945aa13ef160b2626d77b2f6adaf47fea
Repository: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-rs
Published VCS commit: d34658bbb2eb4593ae6df959aa93e9ee1e0457c6, path ts_netmon.

Every imported file matches that archive except src/linux/mod.rs::init_state.
The regression is in ts_runtime/src/netmon.rs. Only Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml.orig and
.cargo_vcs_info.json are omitted. LICENSE and PATENTS match this published archive:
https://static.crates.io/crates/tailscale/tailscale-0.6.1.crate
SHA-256: 7c41f9ac0c6e105ebcb5c368e8636d4926c28ec77aa000ddcc126df1fb527b2e

ts_netmon was already a transitive dependency at this version. Cargo's existing
[patch.crates-io] mechanism replaces crate sources, not individual functions. A Nix-only
patch would leave native Cargo builds and application packaging on the broken code.
Replacing the monitor inside ts_runtime would duplicate the Linux implementation and
add platform-selection logic. Keeping the upstream crate intact makes the maintained
patch just the lazy dump sequencing and preserves the other platform implementations.

ts_dataplane provenance
----------------------
Source archive: https://static.crates.io/crates/ts_dataplane/ts_dataplane-0.6.1.crate
SHA-256: ac692c013513afe18dc7ead7a74f3e67c048f943feae4d01b1c819d7bc445c94
Repository: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-rs
Published VCS commit: d34658bbb2eb4593ae6df959aa93e9ee1e0457c6, path ts_dataplane.

Every imported file matches that archive except the TCP branch in src/lib.rs.
The encrypted-packet regressions are in ts_runtime/src/dataplane.rs. Only Cargo.lock,
Cargo.toml.orig and .cargo_vcs_info.json are omitted. LICENSE and PATENTS match the
same published tailscale archive and checksum listed above.

This was already a transitive dependency at this version. The existing Cargo path
patch makes the correction available to native and Nix builds. ts_runtime's filter
interface receives no TCP flags, so it cannot distinguish replies from new inbound
connections. The correction belongs where ts_dataplane decodes the transport header.

The changes
-----------
peer list (tailscale, ts_runtime)
    Device::peers lists every peer in the tailnet; 0.6.1 only looks one up by name or
    address. The peer tracker also answers at once when a netmap shows the tailnet has no
    other peers, instead of leaving the question waiting.
    Used by: the Tailscale group on the Remote Hosts page.
    Drop when: upstream can list all peers without waiting.

device info (ts_control; struct literals in ts_runtime's peer_db tests)
    Node keeps, as DeviceInfo, the system, distribution and device model a peer reports in
    its Hostinfo; 0.6.1 drops them.
    Used by: the machine icons and subtitles on the Remote Hosts page.
    Drop when: upstream keeps this on Node.

sign-in state (tailscale, ts_runtime)
    Device::current_auth_state, current_self_node and registration_error answer at once with
    where signing in stands; 0.6.1's questions wait until it is done. When control turns the
    device away, the control runner stays in a Failed state that says why, instead of
    stopping with the reason only in the log.
    Used by: the Tailscale panel's status, login link and error message.
    Drop when: upstream offers status queries that do not wait, and reports a refused
    registration.

shutdown (tailscale)
    Device::stop stops a device that is still shared: gracefully within a timeout, else
    violently.
    Used by: thinkterm-tailnet when it ends or replaces its node.
    Drop when: upstream's shutdown works on a shared device.

no panic (ts_runtime)
    kameo 0.21 panics in Context::forward and try_forward when the target's mailbox is full
    or closed. The registry and Env::forward ask from a task instead, so those cases come
    back as errors. Env::ask backs off from 10 ms to 1 s when it retries an actor that has
    stopped, instead of spinning.
    Drop when: upstream moves to a kameo without the panic, or stops forwarding this way.

lost peers (ts_netstack_smoltcp_core)
    TCP sockets get a 10-minute timeout and a 2-minute keep-alive, so a peer that disappears
    without a word (a laptop put to sleep) ends the connection instead of leaving it
    retrying forever.
    Drop when: upstream sets a timeout and a keep-alive on its sockets.

derp dial (ts_derp, ts_runtime)
    A DERP region whose servers cannot be reached, or whose TLS handshake fails, is an error
    for its client; 0.6.1 unwraps the outcome of the dial and panics. A connection gets 15 s
    to come up, as none of its steps has a limit of its own. After a failure the region's
    runner waits and tries again, from 1 s doubling to 30 s, starting from 1 s again once a
    connection held for 10 s. While it waits, what is queued for the region is dropped as it
    comes, and the region becoming home ends the wait. 0.6.1's runner returned on any error,
    leaving the region without a client. A try after a failed one starts with the region's
    next server: the dial goes down a region's servers only up to the first that takes the
    TCP connection, so one that then failed the TLS handshake, or said nothing till the 15 s
    ran out, kept the others from ever being tried.
    Drop when: upstream's DERP client reports a failed dial and its runner retries.

derp frames (ts_derp)
    A frame from a DERP server too short for its type -- a PeerGone without its reason byte,
    as servers from before the reason send, or a packet without its source key -- is passed
    over, and an unknown PeerGone reason only logged; 0.6.1 unwraps the first two, panicking,
    and ends the connection over the third.
    Drop when: upstream's client takes such frames in its stride.

derp reads (ts_derp)
    A DERP connection that has gone 120 s without a frame from the server counts as gone: the
    server sends a keep-alive whenever it has had nothing else to send for a minute, and Go's
    client allows as long. 0.6.1 waited for good, so a connection that died while nothing was
    sent on it -- the machine slept, the network changed -- held its runner, often the home
    region's, and the node got nothing more through it.
    Drop when: upstream's client times its reads out.

derp runner (ts_runtime)
    A region's runner ends with its Uniderp: Uniderp::on_stop stops it, and the runner leaves
    by itself once the Uniderp's end of the home-derp watch is gone. kameo leaves a linked task
    running when a supervised actor is restarted, stops normally or goes down with its
    supervisor, and 0.6.1's runner then spun at full speed on the closed watch for as long as
    the process lived. The runner also ends when the dataplane closes its queue, which 0.6.1
    took for activity and connected over, again and again with no wait. A runner ending while
    its Uniderp lives fails the Uniderp, which is restarted with a new transport; by kameo's
    default the Uniderp stayed up with no runner, and the region had no client.
    A Uniderp that stops leaves its queue to a task that empties it until the dataplane goes:
    routes lead to the transport until they are redone, and the dataplane unwraps each send,
    so a packet coming meanwhile panicked it and it restarted empty. A Uniderp kameo restarts
    asks the bus for the latest DERP latency measurement (RetainedBus's GetRetained::new):
    keeping its actor id, it is not sent what the bus retains, and a restarted home region
    took itself for any other until the DERP map changed.
    Drop when: upstream ties the runner's lifetime to its Uniderp's.

derp regions (ts_runtime)
    A region whose Uniderp failed too often to be restarted is given up on its own, and
    started once more a minute later if the DERP map still has it; by kameo's default
    Multiderp stopped with it, and every other region's client went down too. Given up again
    within 30 minutes of that, it waits twice as long each time, up to 30 minutes, as every
    start takes a transport the dataplane keeps for good; DERP maps that come meanwhile do not
    start it early. A Uniderp whose region left the DERP map stops normally and is not
    restarted (0.6.1 restarted it five times, each taking a transport); should the map have
    the region again by the time it is gone, it is started again at once.
    Multiderp keeps its own record of each region's Uniderp, from its spawn until it is gone
    for good, instead of looking it up in the registry: a Uniderp is there only once started,
    so a map coming meanwhile started a second one for the region, and one gone for good
    keeps its name there, so its region never came back. Multiderp also takes the region's
    transport out of its map itself once the Uniderp is gone for good. Uniderp::on_stop did,
    but kameo tells the supervisor before it runs on_stop: the Uniderp restarted in its place
    could put its transport in first, and out it went.
    Drop when: upstream's Multiderp outlives a region it gave up and starts it again.

netlink dump (ts_netmon)
    Linux permits only one active netlink dump per socket. Initial link, address and route
    requests run in order, creating each only after the previous response is exhausted.
    Chaining already-created streams is insufficient: rtnetlink's execute sends eagerly.
    Overlapping dumps can fail with EBUSY and leave the node without advertised endpoints.
    Drop when: upstream serializes initial dumps, including request creation.

control reconnect (ts_runtime)
    Failed control dials retry with a bounded delay in the supervised registration task rather
    than exhausting supervision and stopping the dataplane. Keeping retries out of on_start
    lets actor shutdown cancel them. A restarted control actor reloads
    retained endpoints and DERP measurements: its unchanged actor id does not receive retained
    subscriptions again. Registration rejection still reports the existing failure reason.
    Drop when: upstream retries control outages without exhausting supervision and retains
    the network state needed by the replacement map stream.

TCP replies (ts_dataplane)
    Apply inbound network grants to initiating TCP SYNs (SYN set, ACK clear), not replies.
    A permitted outbound connection otherwise loses its SYN-ACK when control correctly
    sends no inbound grants. This matches Go Tailscale's runIn4/runIn6 and IsTCPSyn at
    commit 37fc7a7a7260. This is a stateless TCP rule; the receiving TCP stack validates
    connection state. WireGuard authentication, source ownership checks, destination
    routing, UDP filtering and rejection of new ungranted TCP connections remain in place.
    Drop when: upstream permits TCP return traffic without requiring a reverse grant.

build
    #![doc = include_str!("../README.md")] became a one-line //! doc: the READMEs are not
    vendored (the root .gitignore drops *.md). In Cargo.toml, tailscale loses its
    [[example]], [[test]] and [profile.bench] sections, ts_netstack_smoltcp_core its
    [dev-dependencies], and ts_runtime gains tokio's "time" feature. Upstream's proptest
    module in ts_runtime/src/peer_tracker/peer_db.rs is switched off, as proptest is not a
    dependency here. ts_derp loses its [[example]] sections, as the examples are not vendored,
    and gains tokio's "time" and "io-util" features. ts_netmon and ts_dataplane retain their
    upstream ancillary files; their regressions live in ts_runtime, which consumes them.

Tests
-----
The additions above are called from thinkterm-tailnet, so losing one in a merge fails the
build. The changes in behaviour have tests:

    cargo test -p ts_runtime -p ts_control -p ts_netstack_smoltcp_core -p ts_derp --lib

    lost peers     socket_impl::tcp::tests (connect and listen)
    device info    node::tests
    sign-in state  control_runner::tests (the reason given)
    no panic       env::tests
    netlink dump   netmon::tests in ts_runtime (initial links, addresses and routes)
    TCP replies    dataplane::tests in ts_runtime (IPv4/IPv6 encrypted stateless TCP, denied
                   SYN/UDP, source ownership, destination routing and malformed/fragmented TCP)
    control reconnect control_runner::tests (an unreachable server leaves its supervisor alive);
                   nix/e2e.py (direct payloads during an outage and new policy after reconnect)
    derp dial      multiderp::uniderp::tests (an unreachable region, becoming home, a
                   connection that does not come up, the next server)
    derp reads     client::tests in ts_derp (a connection gone quiet, keep-alives)
    derp runner    multiderp::uniderp::tests (a runner whose Uniderp is gone, whose queue
                   is closed, that ended; a region given up; the transport of a Uniderp
                   gone; a Uniderp restarted in the home region)
    derp regions   multiderp::tests (the waits); multiderp::uniderp::tests (a region given
                   up, waiting out its wait, getting one Uniderp, dropped from the map and
                   put back)

Not covered by a test: the peer tracker's answer for an empty tailnet, and the Failed state
taking the place of the stop. Signing in to a real tailnet after an upgrade checks the
first; signing in with a wrong auth key checks the second. Nor are the parts of derp dial
and derp frames that need a working DERP server (the waits starting over after a connection
that held, frames the server sends).

Upgrading
---------
1. Read upstream's CHANGELOG.md for the new version: its security fixes, and anything that
   touches the groups above. A group upstream now covers can be dropped instead of merged.
2. For each vendored crate, merge three ways, file by file: the base is upstream's old
   version, ours is deps/tailscale-rs/<crate>, theirs is upstream's new version. With both
   versions unpacked in /tmp as above:

       git merge-file deps/tailscale-rs/<crate>/src/<file> /tmp/<crate>-<old>/src/<file> \
           /tmp/<crate>-<new>/src/<file>

   Changes that do not overlap merge by themselves; overlapping ones are left between
   conflict markers. Copy files upstream added; move by hand our changes in a file upstream
   removed or renamed. For Cargo.toml, take upstream's new one and redo the build changes.
3. Bump the version: these crates' entries under [patch.crates-io] in the root Cargo.toml and
   the two in thinkterm-tailnet/Cargo.toml, then `cargo update` the other tailscale-rs
   crates to the same version. All tailscale-rs crates move together.
4. Build, run the tests above and thinkterm-tailnet's and thinkterm-tailnet-node's, then
   sign in to a real tailnet and connect to a machine by name and by address.
5. Update this file: the version above, and every group that changed or went away.
